text.p: Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co (Metrobank), the Philippines' biggest bank, on Friday reported a 43 percent surge in net profit in 1996 to 5.003 billion pesos (US$189.9 million).
In 1995, Metrobank had profits of 3.501 billion pesos and Friday's results were in line with expectations.
A Reuter poll of six analysts this month resulted in an average prediction of 4.945 billion pesos in 1996 net profit.
The bank's robust earnings last year came largely from a 36 percent expansion in its loan portfolio to 123.5 billion from 90.879 billion.
As a result, total interest income rose 44 percent to 15.363 billion from 10.684 billion pesos.
"Its earnings are in line with expectations. It provides a good, solid staging point to achieve the 1997 profit of seven billion pesos," said Jose Salceda, director of SBC Warburg.
The bank has set a profit target of seven billion pesos for this year.
"Metrobank must really have had a very good year," said Rico Gonzales, an analyst at Philippine Asia Equity.

He said the bank would have shown higher profits had it not provided such large provisions for possible losses. The bank raised its provision by 60.9 percent to 597 million pesos in 1996 from 371 million pesos in 1995.
The Central Bank requires all banks to provide for possible losses but Metrobank officials said they set aside more than called for under the rules.
Gonzales said he would upgrade his 1997 net income forecast for the bank to between 6.5 billion and 6.8 billion pesos from 6.07 billion.

"The year 1996 was a major milestone for Metrobank. It finally seized market leadership from Philippine National Bank in terms of loans, equity base and resources," said Salceda. "It certainly is a must-have stock in the Philippines."

Metrobank shares closed on Friday at an all-time high 720 pesos. It is trading at 18 times earnings versus Bank of the Philippine Islands' 26 times and Philippine National Bank's 16 times, Salceda said.
He said he sees Metrobank's share price climbing to 800 pesos this quarter, equivalent to a price-earnings multiple of 21 times forecast 1997 earnings per share of 37.50 pesos.
"Metrobank remains our top pick in the banking sector," Angping & Associates Securities Inc said. It projected the bank's 1997 profits to grow 37 percent to 6.847 billion pesos.
Asia Equity's Gonzales, however, said Metrobank is now expensive at 19 times 1997 earnings versus an average multiple of 17 times for stocks in Asia Equity's portfolio.
Analysts said Metrobank had improved its net interest margin to 4.8 percent from 4.3 percent due to the low cost of funding raised through several stock rights offerings since 1993.
